approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. A bounded population supplies score-quantile breeding parents; fresh candidates come from connected-fragment crossover or local atom and bond mutation walks, including the retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity admission builds a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses local-environment occurrence counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance, and correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated batch. Accepted offspring update the full prediction archive and compete for survival and later breeding.
approach.novelty: Remove two-parent fragment crossover and let the existing single-parent mutation walks supply every fresh pool. This tests whether recombination still contributes after the retained nitrogen-position move and count-sensitive posterior are combined. Earlier siblings changed which partners cross or which first-parent ring cores survive a cut; both retained crossover and lost mean score. This ablation removes that route completely, preserving the current mutation operators and learned selector, to test whether a simpler composition can preserve the Parent's performance.

hypothesis: Remove two-parent connected-fragment crossover from fresh-pool production, routing every proposal through the inherited single-parent local-mutation walk while retaining the count-based posterior and correlated batch allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal lowers mean score by 0.02886 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights:
The complete-loop ablation supplies evidence that crossover still contributes to this integrated method on the supplied panel. Its lower observed parent-beating rate was an inadequate argument for removal. That rate compared crossover products with the better of two parents, and both route cohorts had already been shaped by population history and posterior selection. The simpler route makes many small local advances on lower-scoring search paths; more improvements and more survivor reuse do not guarantee stronger endpoints. Removing crossover also changes the opportunities seen by the retained nitrogen move: valid exchange steps increase from 435 to 658, while accepted walks containing an exchange fall from 46 to 27. Local availability therefore does not establish useful allocation after the search distribution changes.

The coverage evidence narrows, but does not settle, the explanation. Evaluated scaffolds distinguished by atom and bond types increase from 1,806 to 1,898, while generic topologies decrease. This is consistent with more chemical variation within a narrower set of shapes. Even the number of generic cores producing incumbent gains rises, so broad exploration loss alone is insufficient to explain the lower endpoint quality. The molecular assessment shows a tighter size range, 21–44 heavy atoms instead of 1–120, alongside an increased median, 33 instead of 29. N–halogen structures and unspecified stereochemistry become more frequent, and bridged or strained heterocyclic families remain. Compactness has not supplied chemical control. Which recombination opportunities preserve productive scaffold relationships, and how their changed populations interact with posterior allocation, remain open. The result does not show that crossover is useful in every generator or that any individual omitted recombinant would have scored well.
finding_summary.results:
Crossover is absent from all 73,389 eligible breeding attempts, all 69,600 pooled candidates and all 4,350 evaluated offspring. All 15 task-and-seed evaluations complete, and the inherited mutation operators, nitrogen-position exchange, accepted-score archive and correlated posterior selector remain active. The three-seed mean final score falls from 0.57434 to 0.54548, a loss of 0.02886 against the registered 0.002 non-inferiority threshold. Every seed mean declines: by 0.06136, 0.00445 and 0.02078. Mean task scores fall by 0.11996 for sitagliptin, 0.01804 for DRD2 and 0.01126 for decoration hopping; they rise by 0.00327 for median similarity and 0.00167 for zaleplon. Seed dispersion increases for every task.

Mutation-only search makes more strict improvements over its generating parent: 713 versus 624 among 4,350 offspring. It also records 286 versus 241 incumbent improvements and reuses 2,606 versus 2,455 nonterminal offspring as later parents. Yet mean absolute offspring score falls from 0.38664 to 0.34884. Generic scaffold coverage contracts from 13,420 to 9,655 in the pools and from 1,059 to 984 among evaluated molecules. Pools need fewer attempts, and internal invalid graphs fall from 536 to two, but there is no isolated generation-speed measurement: the large total runtime reduction comes mainly from recorded oracle time.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatics and cyclic amines have a tighter size range, but unusual bonding and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: The complete seed panel was read for n-1faebb978a01 and Parent n-559d25e9c9c7: all five tasks, seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 trajectory entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task. No tasks lack trajectories. The Child produces connected, branched molecules with substantial ring chemistry, rather than isolated small fragments. Every task has digest ring_closure_rate 1.0; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.8943 to 1.0. These text counters indicate presence, not chemically achievable ring geometry. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 inspection finds 21–44 heavy atoms per Child proposal, median 33, versus Parent 1–120, median 29; mean sizes are 31.7763 and 32.9570 respectively. The Child removes size extremes while retaining sizable molecules. Its 984 generic Murcko cores versus Parent 1059 show real topological exploration, but upper-score cohorts repeatedly concentrate on closely related families. All 4350 Child proposals parse as single connected structures with zero formal charge. Potentially protonatable amines are nevertheless present. The main quality deficit is chemical control: 887/4350 Child proposals contain an N–halogen bond, compared with 745/4350 Parent proposals. Oxygen–oxygen bonds decline from 236 to 38, so the liability mix changes rather than disappearing. Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2818/4350 Child and 2284/4350 Parent proposals; neither panel contains an assigned centre. Conventional aryl ketones, ethers, amides, imides and cyclic amines coexist with N-fluoro/N-bromo groups, sulfenamides, unusual sulfur valences, strained rings and crowded heteroatom chains. This supports questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality, despite recognizable useful fragments. All scores below are supplied observations, rounded where stated. A score association identifies a local chemical trend; it cannot establish the desirability of an unseen pharmacophore. The passive audit, input hashes, descriptor definitions and digest-only structure drawing are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-03-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json, the adjacent .py and .png. SMARTS bond counts are structural flags, not measured reactivity or synthetic success.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals are compact, 21–28 heavy atoms with median 25, and overwhelmingly retain an indole-like fused aromatic unit plus another aromatic partner. The digest has ring and aromatic presence rates 1.0. Seed 0 emphasizes N-halogenated aryl amides/amidines and N–O or N–S substitution on the fused ring; its cited seed 0/evaluation 257 molecule has a methoxy group, fluoromethyl substituent, aniline and N-bromoamide. Seed 1 reaches a methoxy/methyl indole–pyridyl ketone carrying an allenylamino substituent. Seed 2 reaches a related pyridyl ketone with an annulated N,O-acetal ring and ethyl substituent. The latter contains 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings plus the acetal ring, so ordinary compact heteroaryl chemistry is accessible. The allenyl and N-halogenated families are less straightforward synthetic endpoints than that ring/ketone framework.
liabilities: N–halogen bonds occur in 201/870 proposals. The cited N-bromoamide and ring N–S attachment warrant chemical scrutiny; acceptance of their SMILES is not evidence of storage stability or an available synthesis.

The allene in the highest supplied molecule is a concrete cumulated-bond liability to examine. The digest cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.0609; aromatic bridges and ring-opened polyenes also occur among low-score structures.
Local scaffold concentration is strong: all 30 highest supplied scores within seed 0 share one generic Murcko core. Diverse text substitutions can therefore leave the core chemistry almost unchanged.
missing_features: The favorable intact pyridyl-ketone and compact heteroaromatic arrangement is not consistently represented across seed families; one upper-score family instead relies on N-halogenated amides and another on an allenylamine. A stable, varied set preserving the favorable ring and heteroatom arrangement is missing from these upper examples.

The panel gives no basis for declaring a particular unseen target scaffold or nitrile mandatory. The supported deficit is control of aromatic connectivity and substituent placement while changing functional groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide at seed 0/evaluation 9 scores 0.305105. Upper digest molecules favor a less oxygenated, intact aromatic framework: the allenylamino pyridyl ketone scores 0.457265 and the annulated pyridyl ketone 0.456219. Moving the pyridine nitrogen within the latter family gives 0.456219 at evaluations 242 and 263, versus 0.444908 at 256. Ring disruption, extended imine/polyene substitution or abnormal aromatic bridges occur among the lower examples: seed 1/evaluation 47 scores 0.034295, seed 1/evaluation 189 0.024368, and the highly cyclized seed 2/evaluation 31 0.079887. More rings or nitrogen alone therefore do not describe the gradient. Even within the late annulated series, replacing ethyl with methoxy gives 0.262943 at evaluation 299 and an isopropyl analogue gives 0.356118 at 300. Child seed maxima, in seed order, are 0.439907/0.457265/0.456219 versus Parent 0.457660/0.442313/0.448414. The Parent also centers on compact substituted indole-like amides; the Child has additional ketone/acetal chemistry, not a universal change of molecular class.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals span 22–42 heavy atoms, median 35; all have ring and aromatic text features. The upper molecules are nitrogen-rich, highly substituted heteroaromatic assemblies. Seed 0/evaluation 296 has 37 heavy atoms, seven nitrogens, imine/amidine-like links, a tertiary amide and chlorinated carbon substituents. Its ostensibly aromatic bicyclic unit has a bridged topology; RDKit aromaticity does not establish that this geometry is realistic. Seed 2/evaluation 287 has 38 heavy atoms and nine nitrogens, combining pyrazole, triazine and a fused heteroaryl lactone with an N-fluorohydrazine chain and S–Cl group. The complete seed 1 trajectory, whose incumbent is absent from the bounded digest, instead ends in a substituted fused dione/heteroaryl family with an N-bromo side chain; its evaluation 291 incumbent additionally contains an oxygen–oxygen–fluorine chain. These are chemically elaborate, often reactive graphs, with recognizable heteroaromatic fragments embedded in questionable whole molecules.
liabilities: N–halogen bonds occur in 404/870 proposals and S–halogen bonds in 26/870. Seed 2/evaluation 287 explicitly combines N–F, N–N, chloromethyl and S–Cl features in one molecule.

The aromatic bridge in seed 0/evaluation 296 and the cumulated ring double bonds in seed 1/evaluation 20 are distinct geometric concerns; a high ring counter is not proof of a conventional aromatic scaffold.

High-scoring seed 2 molecules carry many acceptor sites but no hydrogen-bond donor in the cited fluorohydrazine family. Dense polar functionality and multiple reactive handles make apparent synthetic plausibility questionable; the supplied scores do not measure those liabilities.
Potential tetrahedral stereocentres are unassigned in 362/870 proposals; the entire digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0.
missing_features: A varied set of stable linkages presenting the favorable nitrogen-rich aromatic environments is missing from the upper digest: imines, N-halogenated hydrazines and chlorosulfur substituents dominate those alternatives.

Nitrile-bearing heteroaromatics occur prominently in a higher-scoring Parent seed family but scarcely in the Child: only 4/870 Child proposals have a nitrile. That marks an underexplored chemical family, not evidence that adding a nitrile itself increases this objective.
The cited bridged aromatic core lacks demonstrated realizable geometry. The molecules provide no route or conformational evidence supporting that particular aromatic assignment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 7 scores 0.548381. Lower optimizer examples include the chromone/polyene/cyclopentadiene-nitrile structure at seed 2/evaluation 11, 0.515327, and a distorted nitrogen-rich polycycle at evaluation 59, 0.517390. Across all three seeds, the higher-score cohorts contain larger and more nitrogen-rich structures than the lower cohorts, but the examples do not isolate one beneficial heterocycle. Seed 0/evaluations 296 and 282 reach 0.614194 and 0.614070 despite the strained aromatic topology. The seed 2 N-fluorohydrazine/triazine family reaches 0.611063; several methylation, halogen and lactone-ring variants tie at 0.609062, while a rearranged, less aromatic triazine-derived ring at evaluation 298 falls to 0.584198. Thus the score tolerates substantial peripheral reactivity. Child maxima are 0.614194/0.587219/0.611063 versus Parent 0.609280/0.619982/0.616992. Parent seed 0 contains very large repeated aromatic assemblies, whereas Parent seeds 1 and 2 include nitrile-bearing heteroaryl and aminoether/heteroaryl families. The Child narrows size markedly without resolving the reactive chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: These 870 molecules have 25–44 heavy atoms, median 36. Rings are universal and aromatic and halogen text-presence rates are both 0.9977. The upper family in seed 1 is recognizably amine-centered: an azetidine or pyrrolidine, an aminoethyl branch, a fluorinated arylalkyl segment and a chloropyridyl terminus connected through sulfenamide, aminoxy or aminoether links. The highest digest molecule, seed 1/evaluation 287, has 31 heavy atoms, a pyrrolidine and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 instead develops fused sulfur-containing cyclic amines with exocyclic amino groups; seed 2 develops bridged amines with thioether and unusual tetravalent sulfur representations. Cyclic amines and arylalkyl substituents look like ordinary medicinal-chemistry building blocks, but the accessory bonding and undefined three-dimensional arrangements make whole-molecule plausibility uneven.
liabilities: Upper molecules include sulfenamides and aminoxy bonds; sulfur-containing final seed 2 molecules additionally show nonstandard tetravalent sulfur written with a carbon–sulfur double bond and two carbon substituents. These need chemical interpretation beyond valence sanitization.

The highest digest molecule has three potential unassigned tetrahedral centres; the fused seed 0/evaluation 300 structure has five. Arbitrarily unspecified stereoisomers are a substantive identity and geometry gap here.

Halogenation is almost universal, and some fluorine atoms sit on saturated linker carbons. Higher score does not itself establish chemical stability, favorable physical properties or a realizable synthesis.
missing_features: The useful amine centres are already present. What is absent is assigned stereochemistry and a controlled spatial presentation of these centres relative to the aromatic groups: every one of the 870 proposals has at least one potential unassigned tetrahedral centre.

Clean alternative connections between the amine and aromatic fragments are only sparsely represented among the upper digest. The tied N–S and N–O examples, and the nearby aminoether example, do not establish a need for the reactive N–S connection.

The strings contain no formal charge assignments despite potentially protonatable amines. They do not resolve protonation or tautomeric alternatives, and the observed scores cannot identify an unshown preferred state.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The strong observable trend is loss of the initial bulky acid/amide/sulfonamide architecture and acquisition of non-amide cyclic and side-chain amines. The 39-heavy-atom acid/amide analogue at seed 1/evaluation 12 scores 0.008243; the polyoxygenated cage at seed 2/evaluation 20 scores 0.011637. In contrast the 31-heavy-atom pyrrolidine/polyamine at seed 1/evaluation 287 scores 0.994023. Its azetidine analogue scores 0.988534 at evaluation 233, and the corresponding N–O-linked variant also scores 0.988534 at 242. An aminoether variant reaches 0.982352 at 277. Across all seeds the 30 upper-score structures retain a saturated non-amide amine according to the conservative structural query and contain no carboxylic acid; the lower cohorts commonly retain acids and carbonyl-rich links. This supports accessible amine/aryl geometry and reduced acid/carbonyl burden as local associations, not a required sulfur bond. Child maxima are 0.982195/0.994023/0.953346 versus Parent 0.995949/0.996455/0.991289. Both panels reach amine/aryl-rich chemistry, while the Child seed 2 endpoint remains concentrated on a distinct bridged sulfur family.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals are relatively large but size-concentrated, at 29–39 heavy atoms with median 35. Ring text-presence is 1.0 and aromatic presence 0.9989, whereas halogen presence is only 0.1379. Seed 0 upper molecules attach a propyl/ethoxy-substituted phenyl and an indole/indazole-like unit to a nitrogen-containing medium ring with imide carbonyls and methylated amines. Seed 0/evaluation 286 has 36 heavy atoms and a 10-member ring; nearby digest examples have 9-member rings. Seed 1 combines an extended fused aromatic/ether framework with an 11-member nitrogen-rich carbonyl ring. Seed 2 ends in more extensively fused aromatic lactam/urea-like assemblies, exemplified by the six-ring structure at evaluation 297. Medium-ring lactams/imides are plausible chemical classes, but these particular crowded, hydrazine-bearing or N–O-substituted ring systems have no demonstrated synthesis.
liabilities: Unusual single N–N and N–O bonds occur in 309/870 and 143/870 proposals respectively. The seed 0 incumbent has an N-amino substituent, and the seed 1 incumbent combines neighboring nitrogens with an N-methoxy group.

A ring of at least nine atoms occurs in 384/870 proposals. These rings are not automatically unsynthesizable, but their conformational and cyclization demands are real; apparent makeability cannot be inferred from ring closure syntax.
Potential tetrahedral centres are unassigned in 699/870 proposals. Low-score polyenes add further unresolved alkene geometry and less controlled conformational freedom.
missing_features: The upper molecules lack a well-separated set of conventional cyclic amine–carbonyl architectures that keeps the favorable aromatic/alkyl/ether arrangement while avoiding hydrazine or N–O additions. The high-scoring simpler ring at seed 0/evaluation 288 demonstrates some access, but most cited upper variants revisit the same medium-ring family.

Assigned stereochemistry and justified medium-ring conformations are absent. The supplied scalar scores do not reveal a missing named target scaffold or uniquely preferred side group; several chemically different substituents tie.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial aryl fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 7 scores 0.167839. Lower optimizer examples such as seed 1/evaluation 27, 0.127558, and seed 0/evaluation 12, 0.138853, carry extended unsaturated chains attached to the retained dione/heteroaryl skeleton. Higher molecules combine alkyl/ether-substituted aromatics with reorganized cyclic amine–carbonyl connectivity: seed 0/evaluation 286 scores 0.245134 and its shorter-ring neighbour at 291 0.244694. A related ring without the terminal N-amino group reaches 0.243262 at 288, so that reactive appendage is not necessary to reach the same neighborhood. The 30 highest supplied scores within each of seeds 0 and 1 all have a ring of at least nine atoms, whereas only one of each corresponding lower cohort does. This is an observed association with a cyclic polar framework, not evidence that enlarging any ring helps. Thiol-, amino- and methyl-substituted variants at seed 0/evaluations 242, 248 and 252 all score 0.239636. Child maxima are 0.245134/0.240689/0.220274 versus Parent 0.222706/0.243215/0.230352. Both retain aryl/ether/alkyl plus cyclic carbonyl motifs; the Child explores more nitrogen-rich medium rings without a consistent per-seed endpoint shift.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals span only 25–32 heavy atoms, median 29, with universal rings, aromatic text-presence 0.8943 and halogen presence 0.8678. The seeds reach visibly different chemotypes. Seed 0 produces fluorinated phenolic/aldehydic aryl groups attached to a fused or bridged cyclic imide cage. Seed 1 upper examples have an N-linked urea/formamide unit, a pyrazole, a fluorocyclopropene and an unsaturated four-member lactone. Seed 2 concentrates on an imino pyrrolopyrimidinone-like core carrying N–F, a fluorinated sulfur ring and a bridged sulfur-containing lactone. Its cited evaluation 225 molecule has 29 heavy atoms, five rings, three fluorines and two sulfurs. These are compact, heteroatom-rich ring systems, but the N-halogen chemistry, strained rings and unassigned stereochemistry make synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: N–halogen bonds occur in 248/870 proposals. The highest digest molecule contains an N–F bond adjacent to imino/carbonyl functionality, in addition to the carbon-bound fluorines.

Seed 1/evaluation 280 combines a cyclopropene with an unsaturated four-member lactone. Seed 2 adds bridged lactones and reduced sulfur rings; evaluation 300 further adds an S–S chain and scores only 0.115908.
Potential tetrahedral centres are unassigned in 768/870 proposals. Ordinary aromatic-ring and atom-count summaries substantially understate this family’s geometric and stereochemical complexity.
missing_features: The observed favorable fluorine and imino/carbonyl arrangement is not reproduced across a broad set of stable, ordinary ring systems. Upper examples depend either on N-halogenated sulfur/lactone polycycles or on a cyclopropene and a strained four-member lactone.

Defined stereochemical versions of the bridged and fluorinated ring systems are absent. The seed 2 highest molecule has five potential unassigned tetrahedral centres, so its apparent compactness does not specify one realizable three-dimensional molecule.
These trajectories do not identify an absent named pharmacophore as necessary. They show that preserving useful fluorine placement while changing the surrounding skeleton remains poorly covered.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 7 scores 0.002094. The unfluorinated aryl/dione/lactone structure at seed 2/evaluation 23 scores 5.789136455227341e-13. Higher families redistribute the aromatic framework and concentrate fluorine while retaining carbonyl and nitrogen functionality. The seed 2 saturated fluorinated sulfur-ring analogue at evaluation 225 scores 0.544777, compared with 0.508038 for the related unsaturated ring at 203. Replacing that carbon-bound fluorine by chlorine in evaluation 296 gives 0.364462, showing that halogen count alone is insufficient. Replacing N–F by N-fluoromethyl gives 0.480746 at evaluation 247, while an N-bromomethyl variant scores 0.168520 at 299. The imino-to-oxo analogue with fluoromethyl scores 0.476491 at 252. These examples support a narrow local fluorine/heteroatom-placement gradient, while the reactive N–F bond itself is not proof of good chemistry. Seed 1/evaluation 280 reaches 0.487517 with a different, sulfur-free but strained ring arrangement. Child maxima are 0.348389/0.487517/0.544777 versus Parent 0.651021/0.487006/0.602525. The Parent upper molecules are mainly aryl-substituted N-fluoro imino heterocycles with fluorinated carbon side chains; the Child adds substantially more bridged sulfur/lactone chemistry in seed 2. That chemical change is descriptive, without assigning the score differences to one feature.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The complete Child panel contains 887/4350 N–halogen structures. Digest upper-score examples include an N-bromoamide, an N-fluorohydrazine with an S–Cl substituent, sulfenamide-linked cyclic amines and an N-fluoro imino heterocycle. Nearby upper-score aminoether and less decorated cyclic-carbonyl examples show that some more ordinary connections are accessible. Bond flags identify chemical patterns rather than measured instability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep favorable ring and heteroatom environments while supplying conventional, stable peripheral bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conventional alternatives for the same attachment environments, with explicit bond-context handling around nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and halogens. Preserve useful ring connectivity and let observed feedback compare those alternatives. RDKit-valid valence and a high supplied score alone do not supply a chemical-plausibility constraint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive inspection finds potential unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2818/4350 Child proposals, including three in the highest-scoring cyclic-amine digest example and five in the bridged fluorinated sulfur/lactone example. Formally aromatic bridged subgraphs and strained small rings add geometry concerns that a ring-closure counter cannot express.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not produce stereochemically resolved versions of its saturated and bridged ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical identity an explicit, graph-derived part of generating and comparing candidates where stereocentres exist, and preserve it through subsequent edits. Treat ring size, bridgehead unsaturation and feasible geometry as structural properties to examine independently of task identity; the present trajectories do not supply preferred configurations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child has 984 generic Murcko cores across 4350 proposals, yet some per-seed upper cohorts collapse to one generic core for all 30 molecules. The digest repeatedly shows halogen, imino/oxo, ring-size or terminal-substituent variants at identical or very close supplied scores. Its overall size range is 21–44 heavy atoms versus Parent 1–120; the tighter range coexists with narrow upper families rather than demonstrating broader useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator explores many topologies but does not consistently maintain several chemically distinct alternatives within its favorable score regions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Seek alternative connected scaffolds and attachment arrangements that retain locally favorable functional-group relationships, and track their coverage separately from distinct SMILES. Maintain multiple chemistry families using accepted feedback, while avoiding a diversity objective that is satisfied merely by ring damage, reactive substitutions or extreme molecular size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 5/4350 Child proposals contain a nitrile versus 261/4350 Parent proposals, while N–halogen bonds occur in 887/4350 Child proposals. The visible upper-score families repeatedly place nitrogen in crowded imino, hydrazine or N-halogen environments. This is an observed coverage imbalance; it does not establish that a nitrile or any one replacement is universally beneficial.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator represents stable heteroatom-bearing functional-group families very unevenly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden task-independent access to stable nitrogen and other heteroatom environments at existing attachment sites, including underrepresented functional-group families, and let the same accepted-score feedback determine their usefulness. Match ring placement and size where possible so that functional-group variation is interpretable without a hidden objective template.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local population of previously accepted scored molecular graphs, sampled through the inherited three score-ranked parent quantiles.

Single-parent atom/bond mutation with unchanged operator weights, bounded inner retries and one/two/three-step walks; saturation-driven longer walks and exhaustion limits remain present but unexercised.
Formula-preserving C/N positional exchange within the same eligible six-member aromatic ring, retaining per-site choice, invariant gates and actual mutation-sequence receipts.
Connected graph sanitization, stable canonical/isomeric admission with graph-equivalent alias verification, initial/emitted/pending/pool novelty exclusions and bounded fresh-pool construction.
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival with admission-order tie breaking and subsequent breeding from accepted descendants.
Full accepted-only task-local Gaussian-process archive, ordered admission history, archive-mean centering, population-SD scaling with floor and fixed observation noise.
Integer-count Morgan environments in the inherited hashed radius-two vocabulary, squared-norm generalized Tanimoto covariance and shared pool/next-fit conditional prediction.
Joint correlated posterior draws over each fresh pool, masked batch maximization, accepted-feedback refitting and next-fit probes; bounded numerical fallback remains present but unexercised.
Disabled connected-fragment crossover, partner selection within that route and optional post-crossover mutation remain as unreachable source code; none executes in this panel.

activation_observables.measurement: Join each accepted score to one pending emitted canonical identity, its actual generating accepted parent, pool record, posterior fit version and selected index, and the next archive and survivor state. finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal lowers mean score by 0.02886 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights:
The complete-loop ablation supplies evidence that crossover still contributes to this integrated method on the supplied panel. Its lower observed parent-beating rate was an inadequate argument for removal. That rate compared crossover products with the better of two parents, and both route cohorts had already been shaped by population history and posterior selection. The simpler route makes many small local advances on lower-scoring search paths; more improvements and more survivor reuse do not guarantee stronger endpoints. Removing crossover also changes the opportunities seen by the retained nitrogen move: valid exchange steps increase from 435 to 658, while accepted walks containing an exchange fall from 46 to 27. Local availability therefore does not establish useful allocation after the search distribution changes.

The coverage evidence narrows, but does not settle, the explanation. Evaluated scaffolds distinguished by atom and bond types increase from 1,806 to 1,898, while generic topologies decrease. This is consistent with more chemical variation within a narrower set of shapes. Even the number of generic cores producing incumbent gains rises, so broad exploration loss alone is insufficient to explain the lower endpoint quality. The molecular assessment shows a tighter size range, 21–44 heavy atoms instead of 1–120, alongside an increased median, 33 instead of 29. N–halogen structures and unspecified stereochemistry become more frequent, and bridged or strained heterocyclic families remain. Compactness has not supplied chemical control. Which recombination opportunities preserve productive scaffold relationships, and how their changed populations interact with posterior allocation, remain open. The result does not show that crossover is useful in every generator or that any individual omitted recombinant would have scored well.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal lowers mean score by 0.02886 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights:
The complete-loop ablation supplies evidence that crossover still contributes to this integrated method on the supplied panel. Its lower observed parent-beating rate was an inadequate argument for removal. That rate compared crossover products with the better of two parents, and both route cohorts had already been shaped by population history and posterior selection. The simpler route makes many small local advances on lower-scoring search paths; more improvements and more survivor reuse do not guarantee stronger endpoints. Removing crossover also changes the opportunities seen by the retained nitrogen move: valid exchange steps increase from 435 to 658, while accepted walks containing an exchange fall from 46 to 27. Local availability therefore does not establish useful allocation after the search distribution changes.

The coverage evidence narrows, but does not settle, the explanation. Evaluated scaffolds distinguished by atom and bond types increase from 1,806 to 1,898, while generic topologies decrease. This is consistent with more chemical variation within a narrower set of shapes. Even the number of generic cores producing incumbent gains rises, so broad exploration loss alone is insufficient to explain the lower endpoint quality. The molecular assessment shows a tighter size range, 21–44 heavy atoms instead of 1–120, alongside an increased median, 33 instead of 29. N–halogen structures and unspecified stereochemistry become more frequent, and bridged or strained heterocyclic families remain. Compactness has not supplied chemical control. Which recombination opportunities preserve productive scaffold relationships, and how their changed populations interact with posterior allocation, remain open. The result does not show that crossover is useful in every generator or that any individual omitted recombinant would have scored well.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal lowers mean score by 0.02886 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights:
The complete-loop ablation supplies evidence that crossover still contributes to this integrated method on the supplied panel. Its lower observed parent-beating rate was an inadequate argument for removal. That rate compared crossover products with the better of two parents, and both route cohorts had already been shaped by population history and posterior selection. The simpler route makes many small local advances on lower-scoring search paths; more improvements and more survivor reuse do not guarantee stronger endpoints. Removing crossover also changes the opportunities seen by the retained nitrogen move: valid exchange steps increase from 435 to 658, while accepted walks containing an exchange fall from 46 to 27. Local availability therefore does not establish useful allocation after the search distribution changes.

The coverage evidence narrows, but does not settle, the explanation. Evaluated scaffolds distinguished by atom and bond types increase from 1,806 to 1,898, while generic topologies decrease. This is consistent with more chemical variation within a narrower set of shapes. Even the number of generic cores producing incumbent gains rises, so broad exploration loss alone is insufficient to explain the lower endpoint quality. The molecular assessment shows a tighter size range, 21–44 heavy atoms instead of 1–120, alongside an increased median, 33 instead of 29. N–halogen structures and unspecified stereochemistry become more frequent, and bridged or strained heterocyclic families remain. Compactness has not supplied chemical control. Which recombination opportunities preserve productive scaffold relationships, and how their changed populations interact with posterior allocation, remain open. The result does not show that crossover is useful in every generator or that any individual omitted recombinant would have scored well.

molecular_assessment.overall_character: The complete seed panel was read for n-1faebb978a01 and Parent n-559d25e9c9c7: all five tasks, seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 trajectory entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task. No tasks lack trajectories. The Child produces connected, branched molecules with substantial ring chemistry, rather than isolated small fragments. Every task has digest ring_closure_rate 1.0; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.8943 to 1.0. These text counters indicate presence, not chemically achievable ring geometry. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 inspection finds 21–44 heavy atoms per Child proposal, median 33, versus Parent 1–120, median 29; mean sizes are 31.7763 and 32.9570 respectively. The Child removes size extremes while retaining sizable molecules. Its 984 generic Murcko cores versus Parent 1059 show real topological exploration, but upper-score cohorts repeatedly concentrate on closely related families. All 4350 Child proposals parse as single connected structures with zero formal charge. Potentially protonatable amines are nevertheless present. The main quality deficit is chemical control: 887/4350 Child proposals contain an N–halogen bond, compared with 745/4350 Parent proposals. Oxygen–oxygen bonds decline from 236 to 38, so the liability mix changes rather than disappearing. Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2818/4350 Child and 2284/4350 Parent proposals; neither panel contains an assigned centre. Conventional aryl ketones, ethers, amides, imides and cyclic amines coexist with N-fluoro/N-bromo groups, sulfenamides, unusual sulfur valences, strained rings and crowded heteroatom chains. This supports questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality, despite recognizable useful fragments. All scores below are supplied observations, rounded where stated. A score association identifies a local chemical trend; it cannot establish the desirability of an unseen pharmacophore. The passive audit, input hashes, descriptor definitions and digest-only structure drawing are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-03-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json, the adjacent .py and .png. The latter contains 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings plus the acetal ring, so ordinary compact heteroaryl chemistry is accessible. The allenyl and N-halogenated families are less straightforward synthetic endpoints than that ring/ketone framework.

The allene in the highest supplied molecule is a concrete cumulated-bond liability to examine. The digest cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.0609; aromatic bridges and ring-opened polyenes also occur among low-score structures.

Loss of productive recombination opportunities and ensuing survivor/posterior trajectory changes are plausible contributors. The larger local parent-beating count uses a one-parent hurdle and occurs on lower-scoring selected trajectories. This metric cannot establish non-inferiority; Parent route subgroups are observational and no omitted alternative was scored.

Sitagliptin supplies most of the macro loss and has large seed dispersion. The supplied chemistry shows different fluorinated, bridged and sulfur/lactone families, but it does not isolate the effect of a particular atom, bond, pharmacophore or stereoisomer.

Chemical plausibility and stereochemical control remain unresolved. Numerical errors, missing provenance, early termination and pool exhaustion are not supported explanations for this result: every replica and every pool completes under the inherited rules.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. A bounded population supplies score-quantile breeding parents; fresh candidates come from connected-fragment crossover or local atom and bond mutation walks, including the retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity admission builds a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses local-environment occurrence counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance, and correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated batch. Accepted offspring update the full prediction archive and compete for survival and later breeding.

Earlier siblings changed which partners cross or which first-parent ring cores survive a cut; both retained crossover and lost mean score. This ablation removes that route completely, preserving the current mutation operators and learned selector, to test whether a simpler composition can preserve the Parent's performance.
